title: How I Audit a Real Estate Lead Pipeline — Stage by Stage, Metric by Metric

sections.label: 1 · TOP OF FUNNEL — LEAD CAPTURE
sections.note: Before judging anything downstream, I map every source a lead can come from and what it costs to get one.

sections.label: 2 · SPEED TO LEAD — FIRST RESPONSE
sections.note: This is the single stage most real estate pipelines lose leads at, so it gets checked on its own metric.

sections.label: 3 · PIPELINE PROGRESSION — NURTURE
sections.note: Right pipeline, right stage, right cadence, checked against where leads actually stall.

sections.label: 4 · CONVERSION — CLOSE & FOLLOW-UP
sections.note: The stage that turns activity into closed deals, measured the same way as every stage before it.

sections.label: 5 · FINDINGS & FIX
sections.note: Every gap gets tied to its stage and its metric, then fixed in order of what's actually losing the most leads.

nodes.label: Map Every Source Leads Come From: Ads, Forms, Calls, Referrals
Check the Metric: Cost Per Lead and Capture Rate by Source
Check How Fast and How a New Lead Gets a First Response
Check the Metric: Minutes to First Contact
Check Whether Leads Land in the Right Pipeline and Stage
Check the Metric: Follow-Up Cadence and Stage Drop-Off Rate
Check What Happens at Appointment Set and at No-Show
Check the Metric: Lead-to-Appointment and Appointment-to-Close Rate
Log Every Gap Against Its Stage and Its Metric
Rank Gaps by Which Stage Is Losing the Most Leads

input_sample.actual: Average first contact at 47 minutes, no SMS sent on new-lead trigger

output_sample.highest_impact_gap: Speed to Lead — 47 min avg first contact, industry benchmark is under 5 min
output_sample.fix_applied: Instant SMS + correct pipeline assignment on new-lead trigger
